ownership_reason: Only the gold computes an entry of the matrix: hop 1 packs the vectorial part, hop 2 places one row per index, hop 3 allocates a row and hop 4 copies the gold's value into each position of the row. The gold's javadoc promises an entry of the matrix of the rotation defined by the quaternion; the variant adds the scalar-part term with the same sign for both index orders, so its matrix is symmetric, not orthogonal, and is the matrix of no rotation. Once the gold has computed an entry, the right value can appear only if a caller re-implements the gold's index-order decision or replaces the gold. The convention is pinned outside the gold: Rotation.applyTo(Vector3D) applies the rotation with a cross-product term whose sign changes with the index order (used in production by Rotation.getAngles, Plane.rotate and PolyhedronsSet), Rotation.applyInverseTo(Vector3D) does the same with the opposite scalar part, and the matrix constructor Rotation(double[][], double) recovers the vectorial part from the antisymmetric differences of the matrix (q1 from m[1][2] - m[2][1], q2 from m[2][0] - m[0][2], q3 from m[0][1] - m[1][0]); testAxisAngle and testVectorTwoPairs (orientation of applyTo), testApplyInverseTo and testCompose pass on the variant.
